questions.q: Describe the major environmental laws and institutions in India.
answer: India has built a strong legal and institutional framework to protect its environment, supported by the Constitution, which makes environmental protection both a directive principle and a fundamental duty.

answer.text: The Wildlife Protection Act of 1972 safeguards wildlife and creates protected areas. The Water Act of 1974 and the Air Act of 1981 control pollution and set up Pollution Control Boards. The Forest Conservation Act of 1980 restricts the diversion of forest land. Above all, the Environment Protection Act of 1986, enacted after the Bhopal disaster, is an umbrella law giving the Centre wide powers. Later came the Biological Diversity Act and the National Green Tribunal Act.

The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is the nodal agency. The Central and State Pollution Control Boards monitor pollution, and the National Green Tribunal, set up in 2010, provides speedy environmental justice.

answer: Together these laws and bodies form the backbone of environmental governance in India.
